newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast gasoline prices ease late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast gasoline prices ease late.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot gasoline prices eased further late Wednesday, tracking a collapse in refined product futures.

An inventory report from the Washington D.C.-based American Petroleum Institute (API) showed West Coast gasoline supplies 2.9 million barrels over year-ago levels on Tuesday, despite a 69,000-barrel draw which trimmed stocks to 29.7 million barrels.
Dealers said sales were razor-thin Wednesday, with poor profits keeping refinery buyers out of the spot market.
The West Coast cash market came under pressure from NYMEX products, which followed crude futures sharply lower after several key support levels were broken during the day.
Dec gasoline ended down two cents to 65.39 cents a gallon, while heating oil slipped 1.59 cents a gallon late.
In Los Angeles, spot refined California Air Resources Board (CARB) gasoline fell a cent to 61/62 cents.
Conventional gasoline in L.A. also fell one cent, reacting to softening NYMEX values.
San Francisco grades moved in line with L.A., at a three-cent discount, brokers said.

Texaco Inc said repairs continued Wednesday on a ruptured pipeline between Bakersfield and San Francisco. The company said earlier it had no information on whether that would disrupt supplies to customers.
